messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — I just reproduced a partial authz bypass on POST /account/link when requests come from an embedded iframe. Repro gist: https://gist.github.com/maria/abc123

Ashwin Patel: Looking now. Can you paste the curl you used?

Maria Chen: Sure — full repro (staging):

```bash
curl -v -X POST 'https://staging.api.redwood.ai/account/link' \
  -H 'Origin: https://malicious.example' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Cookie: session=eyJ...' \
  -d '{"target_user_id":"victim@example.com","link_token":"abc"}'
```

Ashwin Patel: Interesting — server returns 200 and JSON {"linked":true} even when the origin is not on our allowlist. I'm pulling code path.

SecBot: :rotating_light: Alert: unusual account-link attempts detected — 24 hits from 3 IPs to /account/link (7m ago). IDS score 0.78.

Jen Ortega: Sequence: can we contain? Short-term options: disable the endpoint, block the offending IPs, or reject requests with unrecognized Origin + require CSRF/token. Also we need audit logs (request-id, origin, user-id).

Patrick Lee: We don't use Origin to authenticate normally. Might be safer to reject unknown Origin for this endpoint as a quick mitigation. But longer term we should enforce server-side session -> user binding and never accept user identity via headers.

Samir Roy: Found the root cause quickly — code was still honoring `X-Forwarded-User` in link handler. That header is trusted by the internal proxy but our embed proxy is forwarding client-supplied headers. So an attacker can set X-Forwarded-User to impersonate.

Leah SRE: Rolling config change to strip `X-Forwarded-User` at edge for all tenants now (will patch edge rule). Pushing to prod-edge: 1798204680.

Tom Alvarez: Do we have evidence customers were impacted? Any PII exfil?

Maria Chen: So far only staging test accounts linked. SecBot logs show a couple of failed attempts against prod but no confirmed links. Need full log review for user_id correlations.

Jen Ortega: Agreed actions: 1) Full log export (prod + staging) for window 1798204200-1798204780 2) Hotfix to remove `X-Forwarded-User` trust + server-side session-binding 3) Add unit/integration tests to prevent regression 4) Compliance notification if we find any customer account modifications.

Ashwin Patel: Opening hotfix PR now, will remove header trust and add extra validation. ETA ~2 hours. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4512

SecBot: CI: PR 4512 passed tests and deployed to prod-canary at 1798204700 by ashwin.

Maria Chen: Canary verification: sending the malicious curl now — response is 403 and body {"error":"forbidden"}. :eyes:

Leah SRE: Prod-edge config confirmed. Rolling to 100% in 5m.

Patrick Lee: Postmortem owners? Jen + Ashwin + Maria. We should include: timeline, attack vector, blast radius, fix, why X-Forwarded-User was trusted, and prevention (audit + tests).

Tom Alvarez: I'll draft customer comms template in case we need to notify.

Samir Roy: Quick note for devs: never accept authentication identity via headers unless explicitly set by hardened internal proxies and validated by edge. We'll add a lint rule in review process.

Maria Chen: Thanks all. Monitoring for 1h, then we'll start log sampling and write the incident report.

Jen Ortega: Adding task items to security board; will schedule post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
